oneOf.description: System nominal; braking components responding within expected tolerances.
Wheel speed indicates complete stop.
Brake system applying commanded braking torque/pressure.
Brake released; no pressure/torque applied.
Holding state (e.g., hill-hold or standstill stabilisation).
High-priority braking event initiated by system safety logic.
ABS modulating pressure to prevent wheel lock.
Brake system applying targeted braking to mitigate wheel slip.
Braking torque generated via electric motor rather than hydraulic system.
Brake temperature exceeds thermal thresholds; performance derated.
Brake system operating with reduced capability.
A fault condition detected in hydraulic, electronic, or mechanical subsystems.
Brake system unavailable due to fault, maintenance, or power state.
System pre-charging hydraulic or electronic actuation circuits.
Brake pressure increasing toward commanded level.
Brake pressure intentionally decreasing.
System cannot increase hydraulic pressure further.
Low brake fluid detected; operational limits affected.
Pad wear sensor indicates end-of-life threshold reached.
Caliper not moving freely; may cause drag or reduced braking force.
Unexpected hydraulic/pressure behaviour indicating leak or blockage.
Fault in electronic brake actuator or EMB motor system.
System performing internal diagnostics.
System placed into maintenance or workshop mode; altered behaviour allowed.
